prompt: Write 5 short claim log entries by an auto insurance adjuster for a low-speed head-on collision claim. Injury: neck and back strain. The claimant is represented by a lawyer. Start each entry on a new line with 'Entry 1:', 'Entry 2:' and so on. No names, dates or amounts. (Internal reference C-1433; do not mention it.)
text:
Entry 1: Claim received on a low-speed head-on collision. Insured reports the other vehicle crossed into their lane on a curve. Both vehicles driven from scene. Claimant's vehicle has front bumper and hood damage. Photos requested from insured and uploaded to file.

Entry 2: Claimant has retained counsel. Representation letter received and logged. All further contact to go through attorney's office. Requested recorded statement from insured; scheduled for later this week.

Entry 3: Claimant reports neck and back strain following the impact. Treating physician notes soft tissue injury, no fractures. Medical records and bills requested through attorney. Reserve adjusted to reflect initial injury assessment.

Entry 4: Independent appraiser inspected claimant's vehicle. Estimate supports repair of bumper, hood, and radiator support. Total loss not indicated. Shop authorization sent to attorney's office for approval before repairs begin.

Entry 5: Attorney's office sent updated treatment summary showing physical therapy is ongoing. Demand package not yet received. Liability appears clear on the other driver's lane departure. File remains open pending medical documentation and repair completion.
